chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you see the people of doubt and innovation after me, then manifest disavowal from them, and frequently curse them, and speak about them, and strike them, and confound them, so that they do not covet corruption in Islam, and the people may beware of them and not learn from their innovations. Allah will write for you good deeds because of that, and raise your ranks in the Hereafter because of that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on dealing with people of innovation and doubt according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia doctrine of al-Bara'ah (disavowal) by linking verbal denunciation of innovators to spiritual elevation, a practice rooted in the early community's need to preserve doctrinal purity against emerging sects. Scholars emphasize that 'cursing' here refers to public declaration of their deviation rather than mere emotional venting, serving as a deterrent to prevent the general populace from adopting their corrupt teachings. This active engagement with the 'people of doubt' ensures that the core tenets of Islam remain distinct and uncontaminated by bid'ah.
